subtype: Approach: asking a parent to remind him at night [Action]
passage: In the cricket club's changing room, Coach Reena read the list for tomorrow's match: whites, pads, ID card, water bottle. Hemant nodded, but his stomach dropped. Last month he had forgotten his ID card and been kept out of the warm-up. He knew his own head. In the car park, he told his father, "Papa, tonight after dinner, please ask me what I need for tomorrow. Then I'll pack." Papa smiled. "Whites, pads, ID, water," said Hemant. "Ask me." At nine o'clock Papa asked, Hemant listed all four, and zipped the kitbag shut. He was at the gate with everything at eight the next morning.

qa.q: What four things did the coach list for the match?
qa.a: The coach listed whites, pads, ID card and water bottle.

qa.q: Why did Hemant ask his father to remind him?
qa.a: Hemant remembered forgetting the ID card last month and knew his own head, so he felt worried and wanted a helper for this important list. 😰

qa.q: What alternative approach could Hemant use next time, and why?
qa.a: Hemant could keep a written checklist inside the kitbag or pack right after practice. A list does not depend on anyone else being free.

qa.q: How might Papa see Hemant's request?
qa.a: Papa smiled and asked at nine as agreed, so Papa probably feels glad that Hemant took responsibility and asked for help.

grounding: Knowing he tends to forget, a boy asks his father to quiz him in the evening about what he needs, using another person as a memory helper.
